scope: Independent source, lowered LLVM/WASM assembly, input-capture shape, and receipt-binding review; no candidate edits, native execution, or timing acquisition by reviewer

resolvedBlocker.issue: Factory-proven live IDs plus jointly detached offset/length metadata can pass the existing witness with equal zero lengths. Unguarded staging threw TypeError before the original unique-index RangeError.
resolvedBlocker.fix: Adapter catches intrinsic source-view construction and staging-copy errors, leaves source buffers unchanged, and returns null to the unchanged JS loop.
resolvedBlocker.observedReceiptResult: Both decline before the kernel and preserve RangeError: Invalid resolved term content reference index: 0

findings.result: First runStart must be zero and U <= current run-window R. At most one native staging attempt occurs per writer invocation; copied payload 4R + 12U <= 16R. Subsequent offset-driven or row-cap splits use the original JS loop. The alternating 64-row split fixture makes one 280-byte copy and 63 fallbacks; U=1000/R=1 copies zero bytes.

All pointer/count span arithmetic widens to uint64 before addition/multiplication; 4-byte IDs/lengths, 8-byte offsets/result alignment and the entire 24-byte result are checked before reads/writes. Invalid ABI returns -1 without stores. Counts admitted by adapter address arithmetic fit uint32.

ID bounds precede offset/length lookup, offset safe-integer-or-minus-one precedes invalid uint32 length sentinel, and both validations precede the prospective range-split test. Adjacent equal IDs skip exactly the same repeated validations as baseline.

The C offset predicate matches safe finite integer semantics for Float64 inputs, including sentinel -1 and signed zero. Minimum/maximum explicitly preserve Math.min/Math.max signed-zero selection. The exact 4294967294 range threshold and subtraction match baseline.

Frozen lowered code has no stack-pointer references or helper imports and performs all four output stores in the common exit block after relevant reads. Raw ABI intentionally permits output/input overlap; its blanket input-immutability source comment is only true under adapter disjointness. Adapter result occupies [8,32), staged inputs start at32, and source buffers cannot equal owned native heap. Input-input aliases remain readonly.

Candidate invokes the adapter only after the existing per-run factory-origin and concrete/private typed-array witness, with fixed-span override behavior unchanged. No await is introduced in validation and witness/value checks are reacquired after awaited appends. Adapter additionally rejects resizable buffers and noninitial/unbounded windows; no cache of value validity spans an await.

Memory-growth, staging-copy and kernel exceptions return to the original loop. Staging affects only the private heap, so the newly added copy catch preserves original first errors even after partial staging.
This remains a component-only injection. Production module loading, lifetime, initialization failure, memory accounting, and whole-import activation/latency have not been implemented or qualified.

limitations: The capture was from Node24.22.3 with in-memory SQLite and test OPFS, not Chromium; its timing is not part of the new component experiment.
The exact enclosing harness was not located in the focused source/evidence scan; capture writer, worker bridge and tail-probe identities are now located and verified.

Hook snapshots are at _encodeArtifactRecordFields, after run selection. Reconstructing factory objects verifies these fixed data groups, but does not itself establish original WeakMap/descriptor/prepared-range admission at the earlier validation call.

The component can prospectively benchmark this fixed hash-bound corpus with these caveats. Claims of current browser production activation and whole-import benefit require a fresh bound import qualification.
